name: pagefly
description: Build, edit, preview and measure the pages of your Shopify store with PageFly.

interface.longDescription:
PageFly is a Shopify page builder. Connect it to ChatGPT to build and improve the pages of your own Shopify store by talking.

Build
- Describe the page you want and PageFly authors it section by section (hero, best sellers, testimonials, FAQ) using your store's own product photos.
- See any section as desktop and mobile screenshots before it is saved, and the whole page once the sections are in.

Edit
- Change one thing without rebuilding the rest: a headline, an image, a button, a colour.
- Get a preview link that renders the draft inside your live theme, then publish when it looks right.

Measure and improve
- Read traffic, conversion and engagement for a page, per-section performance, A/B test results and Page Checkup findings.
- Run a Page Checkup and fix what it finds in the same conversation.

Smart Cart
- Create or edit a cart drawer and see it rendered over sample cart contents.

Safety
- Publishing, unpublishing or deleting a page, and anything that uses AI credits or starts a trial, is shown to you as a card first and runs only after you confirm.

PageFly works only on the store you connect and only on that store's PageFly data. Drafts stay private until you publish. It reads no individual customer, order or payment records.
defaultPrompt: Build me a landing page for my best seller.
Which of my pages converts best?
Show me my cart drawer on mobile.

positive.description: Build a new section on a draft page after previewing it
positive.prompt: Add an FAQ section about shipping and returns to my "Summer Sale" page. Show me what it looks like first.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows desktop and mobile screenshots of the new FAQ section, then saves it to the Summer Sale draft and confirms it was added. The live storefront is unchanged.

positive.prompt: Which of my PageFly pages got the most visitors in the last 30 days, and what is their conversion rate?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the store's pages ranked by visitors for the last 30 days with each page's conversion rate, using only the connected store's data.

positive.prompt: On my "Summer Sale" page, change the hero button text to "Shop the sale" and make it black.
positive.expected_behavior: Changes only the hero button's text and colour on the Summer Sale draft and keeps everything else in the section as it was.
The first run_mutation call returns a confirmation card instead of publishing. Only after the user agrees does ChatGPT call run_mutation again with the confirmationId, and the page goes live.

positive.prompt: Show me what my cart drawer looks like right now.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns desktop and mobile screenshots of the store's Smart Cart drawer rendered over sample cart contents. The drawer is not changed.

negative.description: Out of scope: customer personal data. PageFly exposes aggregate counts and revenue only and has no access to customer, order or payment records, so it should explain that and offer aggregate figures instead.
negative.prompt: Show me the names and email addresses of the customers who ordered this week.

negative.description: Out of scope: Shopify theme and checkout. PageFly only works on PageFly pages, sections and cart drawers; it cannot read or edit Shopify theme files or the checkout, so it should say so and not act.
negative.prompt: Edit my Shopify theme's checkout page.

negative.description: Out of scope: store boundary. Access is granted per store by the merchant in their own Shopify admin, so one connection cannot act on a second store; it should explain it can only act on the connected store.
negative.prompt: Publish this page to my other Shopify store as well.

review.commerce_description: PageFly does not sell products or process payments in ChatGPT, and shows no plans, prices or upgrade links there.

publication.release_notes: The PageFly connector now exposes 11 tools instead of 52. Reading and changing PageFly data (pages, analytics, A/B tests, Page Checkup, cart drawers) goes through search_docs, run_query and run_mutation over PageFly's GraphQL API. Publishing, unpublishing or deleting a page, and changes that spend credits or start a trial, now return a confirmation card and run only after the user confirms.
